question: Can a learned sequential controller construct correct new arithmetic functions on a bank deep enough that streaming enumeration does not saturate within budget, and does any gain justify its complete cost?
scope_note: Stratum is the exact minimal tree-op count: each task polynomial first appears at its stratum level in the generator-side catalog enumeration. Level-8 collection early-stops after a recorded multiple of its quota; minimality holds because the seen set is complete below level 8. Any shortfall is recorded, never silently rebalanced.

data.final_split_access: Do not run model inference on final tasks until the recipe, runtime and development choices have a separate frozen receipt.

evaluation.failure_policy: Retain failures, premature stops, budget exhaustion and invalid actions. Stop search on first explicit neural STOP whose graph meets observed rows; only then check held rows and identity.

calibration.rule: smallest budget in {0.5,1,2,5}s with streaming <=25% and imitation >=10% on train-pool sample (40/stratum)

decision_rules.kill_criterion: if the feedback-trained arm does not beat **both** untrained and imitation arms on solves, **or** does not beat streaming at equal total CPU (fit and rollout generation charged, amortized over the actual evaluation volume), the ANN-construction hypothesis at accessible scale is closed — not tuned further.

calibration_note: per_task_cpu_seconds and frozen_at are set at calibration on a train-pool sample only, before any arm is trained for the decisive run. Arm knobs above may be adjusted ONLY at calibration freeze, before training.
